rv.q: He can stand still and speak quietly, and hold the whole theatre in breathless silence. Miles and Godley are also fantastic, like the straight man and the comic relief. Miles is a solid, serious presence and there’s some of the casual confidence in him that goes with being a banker.

Only audiences with a thorough understanding of the subprime mortgage industry need apply, you might think. But in fact, this isn’t a hydra-headed, David Hare-style lesson in economic nuance but a lean three-hander in which the hubristic history of American capitalism takes on the deceptive charm of a folk tale.

Es Devlin’s rotating design, dominated by a glass office space, incorporates often dizzying projections by Luke Halls that transport us from the plantations of nineteenth-century Alabama via the Great Depression to the shark tank of modern Wall Street.

London theatre has already offered two theatrical marathons this year, THE INHERITANCE soon to return to the West End, and IMPERIUM, currently playing at the Gielgud Theatre. Both clock in at around seven hours. By comparison the LEHMAN TRILOGY at the National is a mere three and a half hours and can be viewed in a single performance.
